results.name: object_delete_to_network
results.evidence: Loop calls periodic_function_evaluate per node and writes results into object+0x134 / dirty bits at +0x123, identical to object_delete and object_reconnect_to_map; likely a recompute of exported function values at a network-scope transition.
results.summary: Recomputes an object's exported periodic "function" values (used to drive markers/effects) from scratch, as needed when the object leaves network scope for deletion.

results.name: object_delete
results.evidence: Byte-identical per-node periodic_function_evaluate loop to object_delete_to_network/object_reconnect_to_map, writing into object+0x134 value array and +0x123 dirty bitmask.
results.summary: Recomputes an object's exported function values before/at full deletion of the object.

results.name: object_reconnect_to_map
results.evidence: Same shared periodic_function_evaluate recompute loop as object_delete/object_delete_to_network; fits an object re-entering map scope needing a fresh (non-incremental) function value.
results.summary: Recomputes an object's exported function values when the object reconnects to (re-enters) the map/network scope.

results.name: object_attachment_set_callback
results.evidence: Looks up the object's attachment node through the DAT_008603b0 index table, stores param_1 into node+0xb0, and conditionally invokes FUN_004f6b70 when flag bits (node+0xb4 & 0xfe0) are all clear.
results.summary: Stores a value on an object's attachment node and, if certain status flags are unset, invokes a follow-up handler.

results.name: object_disconnect_from_map
results.evidence: Compares the attachment node's +0x14 epoch field against DAT_008603cc, a counter incremented once per traversal in object_get_orientation; returns whether the object was not touched in the current pass.
results.summary: Tests whether an object's attachment was not visited during the current map traversal (i.e. is effectively disconnected).

results.name: object_create_attachments
results.evidence: Switches on each attachment definition's fourcc tag ('ligh','lsnd','effe','cont','pctl') and calls the matching subsystem's *_new (FUN_004f0af0 light, FUN_00543c20 looping_sound, FUN_004506d0 effect, FUN_0044c910 contrail, FUN_004536f0 particle), recording type+handle per attachment slot.
results.summary: Creates the runtime instance for every attachment (light/looping-sound/effect/contrail/particle) defined on an object's type.

results.name: object_delete_attachments
results.evidence: Switches on the same 5 stored attachment type codes (0..4) used by object_create_attachments, calling FUN_004f0bd0 (light), datum_delete (looping sound), FUN_00450be0 (effect), FUN_004f8310+FUN_0044ca60 (contrail), and inline particle-block cleanup for type 4.
results.summary: Releases all runtime attachment instances (light/looping-sound/effect/contrail/particle) previously created for an object.

results.name: object_delete_attachments_tail
results.evidence: Contains the identical attachment-type delete switch as object_delete_attachments but structured as a self-looping goto back to its own start; almost certainly a duplicate compiled entry point rather than a marker-name lookup (no name string or comparison is present).
results.summary: Duplicate/alternate compiled entry for the attachment-deletion loop (see object_delete_attachments); despite its prior name it does not look up a marker by name.

results.name: object_for_each_light_attachment
results.evidence: Only runs when the object's cached 0x100 flag (set by object_create_attachments when a light attachment exists) is set, then walks attachments of stored type 0 (light) calling chimera__light_table and/or a per-light callback FUN_004f2a00 based on the two boolean params.
results.summary: Iterates an object's light attachments, optionally registering each in the active-light table and/or invoking a per-light callback.

results.name: object_reserve_render_cache_slot
results.evidence: Writes the object index (in_EDX) into the first free entry of table DAT_006b8cb8[in_CX] and records the slot index on the object at +0xba.
results.summary: Reserves a free slot in a small render/permutation cache table for an object and remembers the slot index on the object.

results.name: object_release_render_cache_slot
results.evidence: Clears the object's +0xba cache-slot field and scrubs any DAT_006b8cb8 table entries that still reference this object, undoing object_reserve_render_cache_slot.
results.summary: Releases an object's previously reserved render/permutation cache slot.

results.name: object_get_or_create_render_permutation
results.evidence: Validates a cached permutation index against DAT_006b8cbc/DAT_006b8cb8 tables, and if missing looks up the tag block via param_1 and creates+caches one through FUN_004f53a0/FUN_004cdde0/FUN_004f5460, finally reserving it with object_reserve_render_cache_slot (FUN_004f9ac0).
results.summary: Returns a cached render permutation index for a tag/object combination, building and caching a new one on first use.

results.name: objects_garbage_collection
results.evidence: cea-pdb match on strings '%d slots free' and 'garbage collection %scritical (%s)'; body walks the object memory pool computing free-memory thresholds and evicting objects via block_list_compact and related helpers.
results.summary: Periodic object-pool garbage collector that frees/evicts objects when free memory or free slots drop below thresholds, reporting via debug strings.

results.name: object_tree_collect_matching
results.evidence: Recursively descends a per-definition binary tree of objects via child links at node+0x118/+0x114, appending nodes that satisfy an optional filter callback (param_2) into an output array bounded by param_5, returning the running count.
results.summary: Recursively walks a binary tree of objects of a given type/definition, collecting up to a limit into an array, optionally filtered by a callback.

results.name: object_local_player_scan_flags
results.evidence: Resolves the local player's controlled object via FUN_005013a0/DAT_00746f9c, then scans a per-definition flag-word array (object+0x14c) for any nonzero word before delegating to object_get_orientation with the matching bit range.
results.summary: Finds the local player's object and, if any bit is set in a per-definition flag bitfield, hands off to object_get_orientation for that bit range.

results.name: object_get_orientation
results.evidence: Kept prior non-FUN_ name, but the body only walks a bitfield (in_stack_00000024) calling object_tree_collect_matching (FUN_004fa0f0) for each set bit and recursing on the next 32-bit range; no rotation/orientation math is present, so the existing name likely does not match this code.
results.summary: Scans a bitfield of type/definition flags and, for each set bit, collects matching objects via object_tree_collect_matching, recursing across the whole bit range; despite its name it does not appear to compute an orientation.

results.name: object_dump_compare_by_total_size
results.evidence: Used as the comparator passed to _qsort by objects_dump_memory, comparing the field at offset +8 of each record (matches the accumulated 'totsize' column in the dump report).
results.summary: qsort comparator that orders object/definition memory-dump records by their accumulated total size field.

results.name: object_dump_accumulate_stats
results.evidence: Increments per-type/per-definition counters (count, total size, garbage/dead/outside/at-rest/no-physics) whose layout and order exactly match the columns printed by objects_dump_memory's '[garbage/dead/outside/at-rest]' format string.
results.summary: Tallies one object's statistics (size, garbage/dead/outside-map/at-rest/no-physics flags) into a per-type or per-definition memory-dump accumulator.

results.name: object_dump_write
results.evidence: cea-pdb match via the shared 'unknown' string and the printf format '% 6d (% 6d) [...] %s\r\n' also used by objects_dump_memory.
results.summary: Writes one formatted line of the object memory-dump report (counts, garbage/dead/outside/at-rest tallies, and a definition/type name) to a file.

results.name: objects_dump_memory
results.evidence: cea-pdb match; references literal strings 'object_memory.txt', 'OBJECTS BY TYPE', 'OBJECTS BY DEFINITION', and calls object_dump_write/object_dump_accumulate_stats/qsort with object_dump_compare_by_total_size.
results.summary: Builds and writes object_memory.txt, a full debug report of object counts and memory usage broken down by object type and by object definition.

results.name: object_start_animation
results.evidence: cea-pdb hints tie the shared error string "the animation '%s' doesn't exist in the graph '%s'" to unit_start_user_animation/scenery_animation_start_private; this object-level routine sets the animation graph (+0xcc), index (+0xd0) and start frame (+0xd2) fields and raises FUN_004c6920 with that string when FUN_004d6ab0 fails to resolve the animation.
results.summary: Looks up a named animation in an animation graph and starts it on the object, logging an error if the animation is not found.

results.name: object_animation_get_frames_remaining
results.evidence: Uses the same animation-state fields (+500 flag, +0xd0 index, +0xd2 frame, +0xcc graph reference) set up by object_start_animation to compute a remaining-frame count from the referenced animation graph.
results.summary: Returns the number of frames left in the object's currently playing animation, or 0 if none is active.

results.name: antennas_initialize
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint ties string 'antenna' to a saved_games antennas_initialize; calls FUN_005380d0("antenna", 0xc), the standard data_new(name, max_count) pattern seen for other subsystems in this module.
results.summary: Creates the global antenna instance data array (data_new("antenna", 12)).

results.name: antennas_dispose
results.evidence: Sets a dispose-in-progress flag at DAT_008603ac+0x24 then calls data_delete_all, matching the antennas_initialize datum array and the analogous flags_dispose (FUN_004fb4f0).
results.summary: Marks the antenna data array as disposing and deletes all antenna instances.

results.name: antennas_dispose_clear_flag
results.evidence: Clears the same DAT_008603ac+0x24 flag set by antennas_dispose.
results.summary: Clears the antenna subsystem's disposing flag.

results.name: antennas_reset
results.evidence: Zeroes DAT_008603ac if non-zero; a small guarded reset alongside the other antenna lifecycle helpers.
results.summary: Resets the antenna data-array pointer/handle if one is currently set.

results.name: antenna_new
results.evidence: Allocates a 700-int record via datum_new keyed by the DAT_008603ac antenna array, then fills a per-segment vertex/velocity array (stride 0x20) from the antenna tag's segment count (+0xc4) and per-segment lengths (+0x74/0x78/0x7c), matching an antenna's initial hanging-chain layout.
results.summary: Creates a new antenna instance for an attachment, laying out its initial chain of segment vertices from the antenna tag definition.

results.name: antennas_update
results.evidence: Iterates the antenna datum array (via FUN_004d0630) and, for antennas still connected to a valid object, calls FUN_004fae10 with dt clamped to 0.06666667 (30Hz), matching the per-instance physics-update pattern also used by flags_update.
results.summary: Advances the physics simulation of every active antenna instance by one (clamped) timestep.

results.name: antenna_update_physics
results.evidence: Per-segment loop using vector3d_normalize_with_length/vector3d_angle_between_4cd4f0/vector3d_rotate_about_axis and a marker transform helper (FUN_004fb1c0) to bend each antenna segment toward the previous one, i.e. a simple verlet/IK-style antenna sway.
results.summary: Simulates one timestep of antenna segment motion, bending each segment relative to its parent based on marker movement and elapsed time.

results.name: widget_apply_marker_delta
results.evidence: Recomputes a marker's current world transform (FUN_004f6080) versus its previous stored position (unaff_ESI+0x10.. ) and, unless the delta is negligible (three FUN_006391b4 magnitude checks), shifts every stored point in the attached point array (param_1+0xc4 entries) by that delta.
results.summary: Shifts a widget's stored point cloud (antenna chain or flag rope) by the movement of its anchoring marker since the last update.

results.name: antenna_render
results.evidence: Iterates an antenna's segments (count at unaff_EDI+0xc4) computing per-segment delta positions and, when bit 0x44 is set on in_EAX, calls the same debug/immediate line-drawing pair (FUN_00511700/FUN_00511620) used by lightning_render; the previous name 'object_definition_predict' does not match this line-drawing behaviour.
results.summary: Draws an antenna's chain of segments as connected line segments (used for antenna wire rendering), despite its earlier 'predict' name.

results.name: flags_initialize
results.evidence: Calls FUN_005380d0(&DAT_0066e99c, 2); the referenced global resolves (via the .rdata string table) to the literal "flag", and 2 matches Halo's fixed two-team CTF flag count.
results.summary: Creates the global CTF flag instance data array (data_new("flag", 2)).

results.name: flags_dispose
results.evidence: Sets DAT_008603a8+0x24 disposing flag then calls data_delete_all, mirroring antennas_dispose against the flags_initialize array.
results.summary: Marks the flag data array as disposing and deletes all flag instances.

results.name: flags_dispose_clear_flag
results.evidence: Clears the DAT_008603a8+0x24 flag set by flags_dispose.
results.summary: Clears the flag subsystem's disposing flag.

results.name: flags_reset
results.evidence: Zeroes DAT_008603a8 if non-zero, mirroring antennas_reset.
results.summary: Resets the flag data-array pointer/handle if one is currently set.

results.name: flag_new
results.evidence: Allocates a large (0x16bc-byte) record from the flags datum array, validates the flag tag's grid dimensions (rows*cols<0xe1 and rows<0x28), fills a rows*cols grid of default UV pairs (PTR_DAT_006966f8/006966714), and calls FUN_004fb6d0/FUN_004fb770 to set up per-cell constraints -- consistent with building the flag's cloth simulation mesh.
results.summary: Creates a new flag instance and builds its cloth simulation grid (vertex UV grid and edge/shape constraints) from the flag tag definition.

results.name: flag_cloth_init_edge_constraints
results.evidence: Iterates the flag's cloth rows, computing a clamped span for each row and calling FUN_004fb840 twice per row -- consistent with tagging left/right (or top/bottom) edge cells of the cloth grid.
results.summary: Marks the border cells along each row of the flag's cloth grid, used to set up edge constraints for the cloth simulation.

results.name: flag_cloth_init_shape_constraints
results.evidence: Switches on the flag tag's shape field (+4: values 1-4) calling FUN_004fb840 once or twice per shape, matching different cloth-grid diagonal/shape configurations.
results.summary: Sets up the flag cloth grid's corner/shape constraints according to the tag-selected flag shape.

results.name: flag_cloth_set_region_split_flags
results.evidence: Fills a rectangular sub-region of the per-cell diagonal-split table (offset +0x1534, the same table consumed by flag_render's quad-triangulation switch) with a direction code (param_5), bounded by the grid's row/column counts.
results.summary: Stamps a rectangular region of the flag cloth grid with a quad-diagonal-split code later used when triangulating the cloth mesh for rendering.

results.name: flags_update
results.evidence: Walks the flags datum array (FUN_004d0630) and calls FUN_004fbae0 with a nonzero dt for each connected flag, mirroring antennas_update's structure against the flags array.
results.summary: Advances the cloth simulation of every active flag instance by one timestep.

results.name: flag_cloth_update
results.evidence: Computes per-row anchor positions via flag_pole_get_marker_positions (FUN_004fc020), then for each cloth vertex blends a wind offset sampled from a pseudo-random wind-field table (DAT_006b7af4/DAT_006b7af8) using the LCG at DAT_00719cd4, and calls FUN_0050b530 (marker/tint transform) -- consistent with simulating flag-cloth vertex motion under wind.
results.summary: Updates one timestep of the flag's cloth simulation, blending each vertex toward a wind-perturbed target position relative to the flag pole's current marker positions.

results.name: flag_pole_get_marker_positions
results.evidence: For each of the flag's pole segments (count at unaff_EDI+0x54) resolves the segment's marker transform via FUN_004f6080 into an output position array, then (in the flag==-1 branch) builds an edge/interpolation index table used to place cloth vertices between pole segments.
results.summary: Resolves the current world position of each flag-pole marker segment and builds the row-interpolation table used to place the cloth grid along the pole.

results.name: flag_render
results.evidence: Builds per-vertex normals (cross product of grid neighbours) and a triangle index list from the same per-cell diagonal-split table written by flag_cloth_set_region_split_flags, then issues draw calls through FUN_0052b050/FUN_0052b180/FUN_0052b530, matching a cloth-grid mesh render.
results.summary: Builds the flag's cloth mesh geometry (vertex normals and triangulated index list) for the current frame and submits it for rendering.

results.name: cubic_interpolate_scalar
results.evidence: Pure floating-point Newton divided-difference cubic interpolation over 4 (x,y) sample pairs evaluated at param_9, with no register-passed/unaff_ state -- a self-contained math helper.
results.summary: Evaluates a cubic polynomial fit through four (position, value) sample pairs at a given position, via Newton's divided differences.

results.name: vector3d_cubic_interpolate
results.evidence: Calls cubic_interpolate_scalar (FUN_004fca60) three times, once per axis, using four control vectors (param_2, unaff_EBX/EDI/ESI) and shared parametric arguments.
results.summary: Applies cubic_interpolate_scalar per-axis to interpolate a 3D vector through four control points.

results.name: lightning_instance_update
results.evidence: Resolves a lightning instance handle through the DAT_008603a0 datum table, reads its tag block via the +0x224-style offset, then calls lightning_update (FUN_004fce80), a marker transform (FUN_004f6080), and lightning_render (FUN_004fe570) in sequence.
results.summary: Looks up a lightning instance by handle and drives its per-frame update, marker attachment, and rendering.

results.name: lightning_update
results.evidence: Maintains a linked list of lightning segment records (0x6c-byte nodes at object+0x250/+0x254), orders them by nearest-neighbour chaining, accumulates total chain length, spawns new segments via lightning_segment_spawn (FUN_004fdb20) at a tag-defined rate, and retires expired ones (datum_delete) -- consistent with a procedurally-jittered lightning-bolt effect.
results.summary: Per-frame update of a lightning effect: orders its segment chain, ages and retires old segments, and spawns new ones according to the tag's rate.

results.name: lightning_segment_compute_fade
results.evidence: Computes a 0..1 fade value from the segment's lifetime fields (+0x50/+0x52) only when the tag's flag bit 0x08 is set, storing it at +0x58; used inside lightning_update's per-segment tick.
results.summary: Computes a lightning segment's fade-out fraction from its remaining lifetime, when the tag enables fading.

results.name: lightning_segment_compute_color
results.evidence: When the tag's flag bit 0x20 is set, scales the segment's base color (+0x38/0x3c/0x40) by its lifetime fraction into the render color fields (+0x44/0x48/0x4c); otherwise copies the base color unchanged.
results.summary: Computes a lightning segment's current render color, fading it toward zero over its lifetime when the tag enables color fade.

results.name: lightning_segment_compute_position
results.evidence: Uses the object's exported function-value array (object+0x134, gated by the +0x123 dirty bitmask -- the same fields populated by object_delete/object_reconnect_to_map) to interpolate the segment's position and a secondary intensity value across tag-defined ranges.
results.summary: Computes a lightning segment's position and intensity by interpolating tag-defined ranges according to the object's driving function value.

results.name: lightning_segment_advance_time
results.evidence: Advances the segment's lifetime fraction (+0x28) by param_1, wrapping or clamping according to the tag's loop-mode field (+0x22: clamp vs ping-pong), and calls lightning_segment_reposition (FUN_004fde40) whenever the timer wraps.
results.summary: Advances a lightning segment's animation timer by dt, handling clamp/ping-pong looping and triggering a reposition when it wraps.

results.name: lightning_bolt_build_chain
results.evidence: Allocates the tag-specified number of segments (in_EAX+0x24c) via lightning_segment_new (FUN_004fd8e0), linking each into the object's segment list (+0x250/+0x254) and applying tag flag bits 0x02/0x04 to alternate segment life flags.
results.summary: Builds the initial chain of lightning segments for a lightning instance from its tag definition.

results.name: lightning_segment_new
results.evidence: Allocates a segment via lightning_shard_datum_new (FUN_004fdde0) and, using the DAT_00719cd4 LCG, randomizes its offset/period/color/phase fields from the lightning tag's ranges (+0x84-0x90, 0xa0-0xa4, 0xb8-0xd0), matching the initial-chain construction path from lightning_bolt_build_chain.
results.summary: Allocates and randomly initializes one lightning segment's amplitude, period, color and phase from the tag's configured ranges.

results.name: lightning_segment_spawn
results.evidence: Allocates a segment via lightning_shard_datum_new (FUN_004fdde0), sets its velocity either from the parent object (when node count < 2) or by random direction scaled by tag speed fields, and is the segment allocator called from lightning_update's per-frame spawn loop (unlike lightning_segment_new which is used for the initial chain).
results.summary: Allocates and initializes a new lightning segment spawned during ongoing simulation, giving it an initial position, velocity and color.

results.name: lightning_shard_datum_new
results.evidence: Calls datum_new against the DAT_008603a4 array and then validates the returned handle's generation/salt against the array's hash-slot table, the standard 'allocate + verify' pattern used elsewhere in this module.
results.summary: Allocates one lightning segment/shard datum, verifying it against the array's slot table before returning it.

results.name: lightning_segment_reposition
results.evidence: Selects which pair of anchor markers (from in_EDX's node list) a segment currently lies between based on cumulative-distance thresholds, then uses vector3d_cubic_interpolate (FUN_004fcb00) to place it smoothly along the bolt's path.
results.summary: Recomputes which anchor markers a lightning segment currently spans and its smoothly-interpolated position along the bolt's path.

results.name: lightning_render
results.evidence: Resolves a lightning instance via the DAT_008603a0 hash table then walks its segment list (+0x250) issuing FUN_00511700 line-draw calls per segment before flushing with FUN_00511620 -- the same debug/immediate line-render pair used by antenna_render.
results.summary: Renders a lightning instance's segment chain as a sequence of connected line segments.

results.name: object_attachment_get_blended_marker
results.evidence: Blends two copies of a marker-like structure's position/forward/up/scale fields (offsets +0x10.. +0x8c) by a weight derived from one of the object's exported function values, writing the result into a static scratch buffer at DAT_006b8cc0.
results.summary: Interpolates a marker transform between two states using an object function-driven blend weight, returning a pointer to the blended result.

results.name: light_volume_new
results.evidence: Resolves a handle via the DAT_006b8d70 hash-slot table (matching the .rdata string 'light volumes' found near 'antenna'/'flag'), checks the tag's marker/attachment counts, and calls FUN_00536ff0 to add the instance -- consistent with creating a light-volume attachment.
results.summary: Conditionally creates a light-volume instance on an object's marker, based on the light-volume tag's marker count and an optional object-function gate.

results.name: object_function_select_or_evaluate
results.evidence: Returns param_1 unchanged when param_2 equals 1.0, otherwise delegates to FUN_006283c0 with the same arguments -- a small blend/passthrough helper with clean stack parameters.
results.summary: Returns a value unchanged when its weight is exactly 1.0, otherwise evaluates it through a secondary (interpolation/curve) helper.
